text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure is considered high (hypertension) when it is consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg.
You can learn more details about these definitions through the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

snippet_links.text: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure uses two numbers. The top number is systolic pressure (when the heart beats). The bottom number is diastolic pressure (when the heart rests between beats).

list.snippet: Normal: Less than 120 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Elevated: 120–129 mm Hg systolic and less than 80 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 1 Hypertension: 130–139 mm Hg systolic or 80–89 mm Hg diastolic.
Stage 2 Hypertension: 140 mm Hg or higher systolic, or 90 mm Hg or higher diastolic.
Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 mm Hg systolic and/or higher than 120 mm Hg diastolic. This requires immediate medical help.
